title: Latency-budgeted speculative phase splitter with kernel-aware binning
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: Prefill/decode scheduling is our primary lever to trade latency vs throughput while preserving tenant fairness. Current chunk/phase splitters use coarse heuristics (length bins + queue age) and sometimes cause both (a) poor tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants, and (b) throughput loss from misaligned kernel selection when a batch mixes incompatible sequence lengths or attention behavior.

Goal: Implement a speculative phase-splitting policy that 1) assigns each request a small latency budget derived from tenant SLA and recent p99 history, 2) performs a low-cost kernel-aware binning probe to estimate kernel footprint and likely attention cost, and 3) speculatively split or coalesce phases to maximize throughput while ensuring each request's budget is unlikely to be violated. The policy should be adaptive per-tenant and include conservative fallback behavior to avoid oscillations.

Key ideas: 
- Latency budget assignment: compute a realtime budget B = base_slo - safety_margin - dynamic_tail_buffer. base_slo is per-route/tenant p50/p95 objective. safety_margin default 15ms; dynamic_tail_buffer = f(p99_recent). Budgets are capped to avoid negative values.
- Kernel-aware binning probe: a fast estimator that inspects request metadata (sequence length, attention pattern hint, KV cache presence) and returns a small set of compatible kernel tags (e.g., quantized-long, sparse-attn, short-seq-fastpath). The probe must be <1ms and not perform heavy sampling.
- Speculative split logic: If a request's estimated kernel tag mismatches the current head batch's dominant tag and the request's budget < threshold T_split then attempt to route the request to a separate micro-phase or hold a tiny window to gather compatible peers. Otherwise coalesce to preserve throughput. The threshold T_split is derived from head-batch latency projection + stored throughput uplift estimates.
- Admission and fallback: If speculative splitting risks starvation of low-weight tenants, apply tenant-weight decay and soft-timeouts that collapse micro-phases back into the main pipeline after X ms. Also expose a per-tenant knob to opt into aggressive splitting.

Integration points: 
- Kernel selector: the binning probe produces hints consumed by the kernel selection path to avoid kernel churn mid-batch.
- KV cache manager: ensure split decisions respect cache affinity (we prefer co-location of cache-hits for efficiency).
- Router/placement layer: allow fallback to alternate model variant (lower compute) if budget cannot be met without severe throughput regression.

Measurements / success criteria: 
- Primary: 10-20% improvement in p99 latency for latency-sensitive tenants during mixed workloads, without >5% regression in cluster-wide tokens/sec (throughput).
- Fairness: 95th percentile of latency across tenants should not increase by >10% for any tenant compared to baseline.
- Cost: measure GPU utilization and kernel-switch overhead; target net efficiency delta <= +2% GPU time for the observed latency gains.

Acceptance criteria: [list below]
acceptance_criteria: New speculative splitter implementation is behind feature flag and can be toggled per-cluster and per-tenant.
Bench harness shows >=10% p99 improvement for latency-sensitive tenant profiles under mixed traffic (short and long seqs) in simulated environment.
Cluster-wide throughput drop <=5% when feature enabled for canary nodes under representative traffic.
No tenant observes >10% regression in their p95/p99 during canary; automatic rollback triggers if thresholds exceeded.
Kernel-selection churn (unique kernel switches per second per GPU) not increased more than 8% vs baseline after tuning.
Runbook updated with failure modes and manual rollback steps; experiment dashboard created and linked.
tasks: Design doc: detail budget formula, probe features, and split heuristics (owner: Priya) - DUE 2026-03-05
Integrate probe into kernel selector and add hint propagation (owner: Linh Nguyen) - 3 points
Scheduler change: implement speculative-split path + collapse timers (owner: Omar Reyes) - 5 points
Bench tests: create mixed-workload harness and run A/B (owner: SRE team) - 2 points
Dashboard & alerting: p50/p95/p99 per-tenant, kernel-churn, throughput (owner: Analytics) - 2 points
Canary rollout: staged across 10% -> 30% -> 100% of runtime nodes with automated rollback (owner: Markus)
risks_and_mitigation: Oscillation: aggressive per-tenant changes could cause phase flapping. Mitigation: add hysteresis windows and minimum dwell time for micro-phases.
Starvation of low-weight tenants: ensure we track per-tenant credit and allow forced inclusion after soft-timeout.
Kernel churn: binning probe may misclassify; mitigation: conservative default to avoid split when classification confidence < 0.6.
Throughput regression on long-tail workloads: run offline sims with recorded traces before canary and enable quick fallback to legacy splitter.
experiments_plan: Offline replay on 3 representative customer traces (chat-short, assistant-mix, batch-long) comparing baseline vs speculative-splitter.
Micro-canary: enable feature on 1 nodepool and run 48h with traffic shadowed and mirrored metrics collected.
Staged canary: 10% runtime -> 30% -> 70% with automated rollback thresholds on p99 and throughput.
A/B for tenant opt-in: allow subset of latency-critical customers to enable aggressive mode to quantify business impact.
